# Keys & Accounts: what we need and where to get it

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` (never commit `.env`).
Legend: 🔒 secret (server only) · 🌐 public (fine in the frontend) · 🤖 generated by our setup script, not obtained by hand.

**Who does what:** one person creates the shared accounts (World app, Hedera operator, Sepolia wallet, LLM key) and shares them over a private channel. Everything else is generated by `pnpm setup`.

---

## 1. World ID (developer portal)
Where: **https://developer.world.org** → create an app → enable **World ID 4.0**.

| Var | Type | What it is | Example format |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WORLD_APP_ID` | 🌐 | Your app's id; the frontend needs it for IDKit | `app_xxxxxxxx` |
| `WORLD_RP_ID` | 🌐 | Relying-party id; used in the verify URL `/api/v4/verify/{rp_id}` | `rp_xxxxxxxx` |
| `WORLD_SIGNING_KEY` | 🔒 | RP signing key (hex). Signs every request with `signRequest()`. **If it leaks, anyone can create requests as us.** | 64 hex chars |
| `WORLD_ENV` | — | `staging` while testing with the **simulator** (https://simulator.worldcoin.org), `production` for real World App users | `staging` |

Notes:
- `staging` accepts **test proofs**, so never ship `staging` as production. The demo can use the simulator; the World prize page itself says hackathon proofs use fake identities.
- The docs name this key both `RP_SIGNING_KEY` (IDKit page) and `WORLD_SIGNING_KEY` (HITL page). We use `WORLD_SIGNING_KEY` everywhere.
- Real-device testing: the World App TestFlight link is on the prize page.

### 1b. (Optional fallback) World OIDC: only if Spike S1 fails
Where: **https://auth.world.org/portal** (sign in with Google) → register a client.

| Var | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `WORLD_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` | 🌐 | |
| `WORLD_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | 🔒 | Shown **once**, starts with `worldidp_client_secret_`. Auth method `client_secret_basic` (default). |
| `WORLD_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI` | 🌐 | Must be an exact registered **HTTPS** URL, so for local dev use a tunnel (cloudflared/ngrok) |

## 2. Hedera testnet
Where: **https://portal.hedera.com** → sign up → create a **testnet ECDSA** account. It is auto-funded with 1000 test HBAR.
Copy the **Account ID** and the **DER-encoded private key** (starts with `303…`).

| Var | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `HEDERA_NETWORK` | — | `testnet` |
| `HEDERA_OPERATOR_ID` | 🔒* | Our platform account `0.0.x`: pays fees for account creation, HCS messages and scheduled tx |
| `HEDERA_OPERATOR_KEY` | 🔒 | Its ECDSA private key (DER) |
| `LEASH_SERVER_COSIGN_KEY` | 🔒🤖 | The server's share of every vault's 2-of-3 key. Generated by `pnpm setup`. **Must not be the operator key** (separation of duties). |
| `HEDERA_MIRROR_URL` | 🌐 | `https://testnet.mirrornode.hedera.com` |
| `HEDERA_USDC_TOKEN_ID` | 🌐 | `0.0.429274` (USD Coin, 6 decimals, checked on the testnet mirror node) |
| `HCS_AUDIT_TOPIC_ID` | 🌐🤖 | Created by `pnpm setup` (no admin key → immutable topic; submit key = operator) |
| `X402_FACILITATOR_URL` | 🌐 | `https://api.testnet.blocky402.com` (fee payer `0.0.7162784`). Fallbacks: `https://x402.org/facilitator` (fee payer `0.0.9185802`), `https://testnet.facilitator.launa.dev`. All three report `hedera:testnet` support on `/supported` as of Nov 5. |

\* An account ID isn't secret, but keep it next to its key.

Testnet USDC: try **https://faucet.circle.com** (choose Hedera testnet; this needs checking, Spike S4). If unavailable, run payments in HBAR (`asset 0.0.0`).
Extra test HBAR: https://portal.hedera.com/faucet.

## 3. Demo merchant (x402 seller)
A **second** Hedera testnet account, so payments visibly go to someone else on HashScan.

| Var | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `MERCHANT_ACCOUNT_ID` | 🌐 | The `payTo` account for the demo paid API |
| `MERCHANT_PRIVATE_KEY` | 🔒 | Only needed to associate USDC / withdraw (can be auto-created by setup) |
| `ATTACKER_ACCOUNT_ID` | 🌐🤖 | Third account used by the "attacker" endpoint in the demo |

### Model backends (`AGENT_MODEL` / `--models`)
| Spec | Backend | Cost |

| `cli:haiku`, `cli:sonnet`, `cli:opus` | `claude -p` using your Claude Code login (Pro/Max). Tools are served over MCP, Claude Code's own tools and system prompt are replaced. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is stripped from its env so it can't bill a key. | Free; uses your plan's usage limits |
| `github:openai/gpt-4.1-mini`, `github:openai/gpt-4.1` | GitHub Models | Free (daily request limits) |
| `groq:qwen/qwen3-32b`, `groq:llama-3.1-8b-instant` | Groq | Free tier |
| `gemini:gemini-2.5-flash` | Google AI Studio (OpenAI-compatible endpoint) | Free tier |
| `openrouter:<model>:free` | OpenRouter | Free models |
| `ollama:qwen2.5:3b` | local Ollama | Free (this laptop has no GPU: slow) |
| `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5` | Claude API | Paid per token |

## 5. ENSv2 (Ethereum Sepolia)
| Var | Type | Where / what |
|---|---|---|
| `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL` | 🔒 | Free key from **Alchemy** (https://dashboard.alchemy.com). Use the **`eth-sepolia`** URL, not `eth-mainnet` (`scripts/check-keys.ts` catches this). |
| `ENS_OPERATOR_PRIVATE_KEY` | 🔒 | A **fresh** Sepolia EOA used only for this project, funded with ~0.05 Sepolia ETH from a faucet. It owns the parent name and is the only writer of agent records. |
| `ENS_PARENT_NAME` | 🌐 | `leash.eth` (registered on ENSv2 Sepolia on Nov 6) |
| `ENS_RESOLVER` | 🌐🤖 | Our PermissionedResolver, written by `npx tsx scripts/setup-ens.ts` |
| `ENS_CHAIN_ID` | 🌐 | `11155111` |

`scripts/setup-ens.ts` (safe to re-run) deploys our PermissionedResolver via ENSv2's VerifiableFactory, registers the parent on the ENSv2 ETHRegistrar (commit, 60 s, register; paid in MockUSDC, which anyone can mint) and checks a test record resolves through the Universal Resolver.

**Design:** agents are `<label>.leash.eth` text records on our resolver, found by ENSIP-10 wildcard resolution. No per-agent registration: one Sepolia tx per agent, written in the background so agent creation never waits on Sepolia. Only Leash's operator can write them, so an agent can't edit its own identity. Revoke sets `leash.status=revoked` and clears the wallet records. Contract addresses and ABIs: `packages/ens/src/ensv2.ts` (from docs.ens.domains/learn/deployments and ensdomains/contracts-v2).

## Safety rules for the team
1. `.env` is git-ignored. If a secret is ever committed, **rotate it**; deleting the commit isn't enough.
2. Testnet only. Never put a mainnet key in this project.
3. Variables the frontend reads must be prefixed `NEXT_PUBLIC_` and be 🌐 only: `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORLD_APP_ID`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.
4. The agent key and the server co-sign key must be **different processes and different keys**. That separation is the whole security argument.
